clue.text: Look at article, ending back where it started

parts.note: lo is an old word for look or behold
an op-ed is a newspaper opinion article

explanation.surface: Someone studies an article that comes full circle, finishing where it began.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that went round in a loop has returned to its starting point, a circular route.

clue.text: Nameless, Dylan's fancy woman

indicators.note: fancy as a verb of imagination suggests the letters being reworked freely

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for name, and the word says that letter is missing from the fodder

explanation.surface: Bob Dylan's girlfriend goes unnamed.
explanation.walkthrough: Take N (name) out of DYLAN and rearrange the remaining DYLA. The surface nods to Dylan's song Lay Lady Lay.
explanation.definitionFit: A lady is a polite term for any woman, especially a well-mannered female.

clue.text: No joke, small island's flipping cactus

parts.note: no means nil or nought, the letter O
a pun is a joke on words

indicators.note: flipping turns the island word over, so it is read backwards

parts.note: an ait is a small river island, as on the Thames

explanation.surface: An exasperated speaker insists it is no joke, referring to some small island's blasted cactus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipping' looks like a mild oath in the surface but reverses AIT into TIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Opuntia is the genus of prickly pear cacti, a botanical name for these spiny plants.

clue.text: Regularly get real fur? Can be cancelled

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of the words get real, here the second, fourth and sixth

parts.note: taken as written: the even letters give E, R, A
sable is a prized dark fur

explanation.surface: Someone urges a reality check about real fur, wondering whether an order for it can be called off.
explanation.definitionFit: Something erasable can be rubbed out or deleted, so it is able to be cancelled.

clue.text: Meddler last to speak one piece, almost nothing

indicators.note: last to picks the final letter of the word speak

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a bit is a piece

indicators.note: almost means the final letter of the word for nothing is cut off

parts.note: zero means nothing

explanation.surface: A busybody who always speaks last offers a piece worth almost nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: A kibitzer, from Yiddish, is an onlooker who offers unwanted advice, especially at a card game.
explanation.definitionFit: A kibitzer is an interfering onlooker giving unasked-for advice, a classic busybody.

clue.text: Daydreaming concealed nervousness, so to speak

indicators.note: so to speak signals that the phrase is said aloud and heard as another word

parts.note: nervousness kept hidden is inner tension

explanation.surface: A daydreamer was secretly anxious, in a manner of speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: Inner tension, said in a relaxed British accent, sounds the same as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Daydreaming means paying no heed to what is going on, a lack of focus or attention.

clue.text: Tax situation Imogen's on top of

indicators.note: in a down clue on top of places the first piece above the second

parts.note: Imogen is the setter, so Imogen's is I'm, I am
a post is a job or situation

explanation.surface: The setter talks of a tax on the job she sits on top of.
explanation.definitionFit: An impost is a tax or duty levied, especially on imported goods.

clue.text: Disciples' dad was like a jack-in-the-box

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the father of the apostles James and John
second meaning: ... in The Magic Roundabout is a spring-mounted figure who bounces in like a jack-in-the-box

explanation.walkthrough: The Magic Roundabout was a children's TV show; several of this puzzle's answers are its characters.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical fisherman and the bouncing children's TV character share the same name.

clue.text: Leave tree, sick, to pick up again

indicators.note: sick suggests the letters are unwell and out of their right arrangement

explanation.surface: A sick creature leaves its tree, to be lifted up again.
explanation.definitionFit: To re-elevate is to raise or lift something once more after it has dropped.

clue.text: Girl put on make-up, half for the dog

indicators.note: put on means the girl is set after the preceding letters

parts.note: to make is to do, as in do a drawing

indicators.note: half means only the first of the two letters of the word up is kept

parts.note: taken as written, then halved
gal is an informal word for a girl

explanation.surface: A girl applies her make-up, partly for the benefit of the dog.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphen in 'make-up' is a disguise: the two halves work separately. Dougal is the shaggy dog in the British children's TV show The Magic Roundabout.
explanation.definitionFit: The Magic Roundabout's long-haired, sugar-loving canine character bears this name.

clue.text: With software installed, organised data can be taken advantage of

indicators.note: installed means placed within, so the software goes inside the table

parts.note: a table is data organised in rows and columns
an app is a piece of software

explanation.surface: Once the right program is installed, neatly arranged data can be exploited.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tappable can be tapped, that is drawn on or exploited as a resource.

clue.text: Honest heterosexual a miserable item, oddly

parts.note: straight is slang for heterosexual
sad means miserable

indicators.note: oddly takes the first and third letters of the word item

parts.note: its odd letters are I and E

explanation.surface: An honest straight man is part of an unhappy couple, strangely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'item' in the surface is a couple; here it just yields its odd letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Straight as a die is an idiom for someone completely upright and trustworthy.

clue.text: Front of gut enormous, all to do with fine dining

definitions.text: all to do with fine dining

indicators.note: front of picks the opening letter of the word gut

parts.note: astronomic, like astronomical, means enormous

explanation.surface: A huge belly comes from a life devoted to fine dining.
explanation.definitionFit: Gastronomic describes good eating and the art of fine food, a gourmet's concerns.

clue.text: Deactivated antibodies — there are seven of them

parts.note: dead means switched off or deactivated
lysins are antibodies that destroy cells

explanation.surface: A lab note says some antibodies have been neutralised, and counts seven.
explanation.definitionFit: Christian tradition lists seven cardinal sins, such as pride, greed and envy.

clue.text: Lawyer's task cut short

parts.note: to dock is to cut, as with pay or a tail
brief means short

explanation.surface: A barrister's job is curtailed.
explanation.walkthrough: A dock brief is a case a barrister takes on directly for a prisoner in the dock.
explanation.definitionFit: A dock brief is a legal assignment given to a barrister by a defendant in court.

clue.text: Divine person in Hard Times

parts.note: H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard
an era is a time or age

explanation.surface: A saintly figure appears in Dickens's novel Hard Times.
explanation.definitionFit: Hera was the queen of the Greek gods, so a goddess.

clue.text: Dump character on carpet with a number of bloody marks

indicators.note: in a down clue on places the first piece above the next

parts.note: Stig is the caveman hero of the children's book Stig of the Dump
a mat is a small carpet

explanation.surface: Someone dumps a figure onto a rug that is spotted with blood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dump' looks like a verb but is part of a book title: Stig of the Dump is a classic British children's novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Stigmata are marks resembling Christ's crucifixion wounds, which may bleed.

clue.text: The point of college: competitive advantage

parts.note: a USP, unique selling point, is what gives a product the edge

explanation.surface: The purpose of a college is to give students an edge.
explanation.definitionFit: A cusp is a pointed end, as on a tooth or where two curves meet.

clue.text: Affirmed as shabby, in a way, and old

indicators.note: in places the shabby word within the way

parts.note: ST, street, is a way
worn means shabby

explanation.surface: Someone confirms an old street is shabby in a way.
explanation.definitionFit: Sworn to means declared on oath, confirmed solemnly as true.

clue.text: Ever extremely fresh and impertinent, the cow

indicators.note: extremely takes the extreme letters, first and last, of the word Ever

parts.note: mint means fresh, as in mint condition
rude means impertinent

explanation.surface: Someone calls a forever cheeky woman a cow.
explanation.walkthrough: Ermintrude is the cow in the children's TV show The Magic Roundabout; 'the cow' sounds like an insult.
explanation.definitionFit: The Magic Roundabout's flower-chewing bovine character bears this name.

clue.text: Making progress on this, say, you criticise party in Ireland

parts.note: U is text shorthand for you
to pan is to criticise harshly
the DUP is the Democratic Unionist Party of Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: A speaker tells you to keep improving and to slam an Irish party.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition completes the idiom: someone doing well is on the up-and-up.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on the up-and-up means steadily improving or rising, an idiom for progress.

clue.text: Attach instruction for placing notice

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to stick or attach
second meaning: read as two words it tells you to put an advert in this spot

explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as AD HERE and it is an instruction for where an advertisement goes.
explanation.definitionFit: To adhere is to stick fast, which is what attaching something does.

clue.text: Enormous snail keeps doing manoeuvres around black horse

indicators.note: keeps means holds within, so the snail's name surrounds the rest

parts.note: Brian is the snail in The Magic Roundabout

indicators.note: around places the rearranged word about the letter for black
manoeuvres suggests the letters of doing are moved about

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
a nag is a horse

explanation.surface: A huge snail is busy moving about a dark horse.
explanation.walkthrough: Brian is the snail in The Magic Roundabout, a British children's TV show. Brobdingnag is the giants' land in Gulliver's Travels.
explanation.definitionFit: Brobdingnag is the land of giants in Gulliver's Travels, so the adjective means gigantic.

clue.text: Next in line making sound impression

indicators.note: sound tells us the word is heard, giving a word spelt differently

parts.note: an air is an impression or manner, as in an air of confidence

explanation.surface: The next in line makes a convincing impression.
explanation.definitionFit: An heir is the person due to succeed to a title or estate.

clue.text: Streams of particles working into metal girders

indicators.note: into places working inside the girders

parts.note: I-beams are steel girders with an I-shaped section
on means working, as of a machine

explanation.surface: Particle streams are put to work on metal beams.
explanation.definitionFit: An ion beam is a directed stream of charged atoms.

clue.text: Game's not worth such feeble power

definitions.meaning: first meaning: from the saying the game is not worth the ..., said of an effort not worth its cost
second meaning: a ... gives a feeble light, and the ... was a unit of luminous power

explanation.walkthrough: The first part is an idiom with the answer missing from its end.
explanation.definitionFit: A candle's small flame is a weak light source, and candlepower measures luminous intensity.

clue.text: Girl's surprised expression, breaking barrier

indicators.note: breaking into means the exclamation splits the barrier

parts.note: a fence is a barrier
lor is a dialect exclamation of surprise, short for Lord

explanation.surface: A girl's shocked cry breaks through a barrier.
explanation.walkthrough: Florence is also the girl in The Magic Roundabout.
explanation.definitionFit: Florence is a female given name, such as Florence Nightingale's.

clue.text: Joker swallows small stone

indicators.note: swallows means takes inside, so small goes into the joker

parts.note: a japer is one who japes, a joker

explanation.surface: A clown gulps down a little pebble.
explanation.definitionFit: Jasper is an opaque, usually red, quartz used as a semi-precious gem.
